scenes.narration: [HL 1] A string with two spaces at each end. [HL 2] Strip removes the spaces at both ends. We get Goa Beach, with nothing around it. [HL 3] Upper makes every letter a capital. scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: strings cannot be changed in place
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the Python error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. We try to change the first letter of the string. Python says, type error. A str object does not support item assignment. Strings are immutable. Their letters can never be changed in place. Instead, make a new string with a method like capitalize, and tie the name to it.

shorts.title: String methods
shorts.hook: "A method is a tool that belongs to a value."
shorts.script: A method is a tool that belongs to a value. You write the string, a dot, the method name, and brackets. Upper makes capitals. Lower makes small letters. Strip removes spaces from the ends. Replace swaps one piece of text for another. These four tools clean almost any text. You use them in nearly every program. Try it in your own file and watch what happens. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Four tools for text.

shorts.title: Split and join
shorts.script: Split and join are partners. Split cuts a string at its spaces, and gives you a list of words. Join does the reverse. It glues a list of words into one string, with a separator you choose between them. So split a sentence, work on each word, and join it back. That small recipe powers search, counting and cleaning. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Cut and glue.

shorts.title: New string every time
shorts.hook: "Here is the key fact about string methods."
shorts.script: Here is the key fact about string methods. They never change the original string. Upper does not make your old string uppercase. It returns a brand new string. The old one keeps its capitals, its spaces, everything. To keep the new version, tie it to a name. Text equals text dot strip. That is the pattern to follow. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Methods return new strings.

shorts.title: Item assignment error
shorts.script: A common bug. You want to change one letter of a string, so you write name, bracket zero, equals G. Python says, type error, str object does not support item assignment. Strings are immutable. You can never change a letter in place. Make a new string with a method like capitalize, and tie your name to it. Then run it, and compare with what you predicted. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Strings are immutable.

shorts.hook: "Why did the string go to the tailor?"
shorts.script: Why did the string go to the tailor? It needed a new method, not a change. Your challenge. Take the text keep coding, with two spaces on each side. Strip the spaces, and print it in capital letters. You can chain the two methods in one line, one after the other. Post your answer in the comments below. Keep coding, says Xecxec! Full video: EP 23.
